Some checks raised a flag. Read the points below before trusting this map.

What the checks found

  • Triangle: the 3 models agree moderately in the chosen layer order (median corr 0.25); maps read in the other order agree with them only weakly (median corr 0.07, 27% of that). The other order keeps a lot of the same structure; check the layer order.
  • Alignment: ink9 is shifted by (1, -4) px against the others. The windowed check will read that as disagreement; register the maps first.
  • Windows, ink9: only 1 windows with strokes above the wrong-order floor, too few to judge (0 not supported). This model sees almost nothing here.
  • Windows, rv2: 8 of 94 windows with strokes are NOT supported by the other models (9%). In the sealed tests, untouched maps were at 0-3% on training segments and 0-7% on held-out ones.
  • Windows, rv3: 9 of 111 windows with strokes are NOT supported by the other models (8%). In the sealed tests, untouched maps were at 0-3% on training segments and 0-7% on held-out ones.

Window by window

seen by the other models only this map shows it barely fades in the other layer order (depth, informative) no colour: not judged (no strokes above the other-order floor)

An alarm means "the other models do not see this", not "this is fake". These checks measure agreement between models, so an ink pattern that every model shares passes (and models trained on the same data share more). Real ink has depth and usually fades when the same model reads the layers in the other order; that depth measure is shown for information only, no threshold has been validated.
